utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-02-60-T, the Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning, everybody. Good morning, Witness. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please stand up and make the solemn declaration in accordance with the paper the usher is showing to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please. Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. Could you please tell us what your name is.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Dragomir Zekic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us your last name letter by letter.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Z-e-k-i-c.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zekic. July 1995, were you a member of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would you please tell us what your position was within the Bratunac Brigade back in July 1995.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: The commander of the 3rd Infantry Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And for how long had you been the commander of the 3rd Infantry Battalion of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: About 15 months.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would you please tell us what training, if any, you received in order to achieve that position, that is, the commander of the 3rd Infantry Battalion.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What kind of training did you receive?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: The centre of military schools in Banja Luka, 1993 to 1994, the 28th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, prior to going to Banja Luka to that military school, were you with the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: For how long had you been with the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Since the end of June 1992 to the beginning of July 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And what positions did you hold within the brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: The komandir of the platoon, komandir of the platoon and deputy company commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: As part of the commander, were you mobilised as part of the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Will you please tell us when you were mobilised and for how long did you serve.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: From the 18th of April, 1992, to the 15th of -- I was wounded on the 15th of May, 1992. From the 15th of May, 1992, to the 20th of -- 25th of June, 1992, I was treated at the military hospital in Sokolac. And on the 26th of June, I came to Bratunac, 1992, that is. I was wounded at Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Where exactly were you wounded, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: I was wounded in front of my native house 4 kilometres away from Srebrenica, the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And what, if anything, were you doing when you were wounded?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: I wasn't doing anything. I was just standing in front of my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would you please tell us what happened. On the 15th, at 5.15, the Territorial Defence of the BH launched an all-out attack on Serbian villages. In a single day on the 15th of May, 1992, 178 houses were set fire to, over 30 civilians were killed, and there were tens or dozens of wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Zekic, where do you live today?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Today, I live in my parental home in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And what do you do for a living?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: I am the deputy director of the utilities company in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And could you please just tell us what is the level of your education.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: I have higher vocational education.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In what field?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: In the field of economics.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, I want to begin where we began this morning, and that is July 1995. Did you, since you were the commander of the 3rd Battalion of the Bratunac Brigade, did you participate in the attack against Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Not in an active attack on Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But were you at that period of time mobilised and on the line?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would you please tell us when it was that you learned that there would be this attack against Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure of the date, the 3rd or 4th, I believe of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And how did you come to learn of this attack?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: I was called to the brigade command.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, when you were called to the brigade command on the 3rd or the 4th of July, 1995, what did you learn and from whom?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Specifically, I received an assignment from the then-commander Milenko Zivanovic, corps commander he was, to reconnoitre the positions in front of me and to make passages in front of the minefields in front of my defence lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, step by step. The first aspect, what exactly were you being asked to do?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: In concrete terms, to indicate the deployment and positions of the BH army in front of our first lines of defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And how were you to do that, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: On a map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, what about the latter part, which was to demine, as I understand, a passage in front of your line.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, I take it -- well, were you given a location, an exact location?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, before we go any further, could you please tell us the make-up of the 3rd Battalion of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Six infantry companies.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now -- and how many men were in each company?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: On an average, 70 men to 75.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would you please tell us whether all six companies were there on July 6th, 1995, the day when Srebrenica was attacked.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: How many companies were there with the 3rd Battalion?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Four.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would you please tell us where the other two were located and the reasons why they were not there on the line on this very important day, 6 July 1995, the day when Srebrenica was attacked.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: One was at Trnovo and another at Stublic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to show you a document and I would like you to look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And for the record, I am showing the gentleman what has come into evidence as P406, and he will be looking at 406/B, which is the original in Srpski.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please look at that, sir, just very briefly first, and then I'll direct you to the appropriate section.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise this, sir, this document.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what it is.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: It is an order for active combat operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, I want to direct -- and what is the date on this document, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And so if I understand your previous testimony, this order would have come after that meeting, whether it was on the 3rd or the 4th of July, for the preparation. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, if you could look at paragraph 5.3, that would be on page 3 of the English version. Please look at it, sir. And please tell us whether this particular paragraph relates to your battalion.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to go through it step by step, line by line, and sometimes word by word so you can give us your understanding of the orders pertaining to your particular battalion. The first line reads: "The 3rd Battalion with its main forces will carry out persistent (decisive) defence of its current positions and secure the introduction of attack forces along the lines of the attack." First of all, what are we talking about when we say here: "Its main forces," the battalion's main forces?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: The main forces of the battalion was in defence at the lines reached from April 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now it says: "It will carry out persistent (decisive) defence of its current positions ..." What did you understand that to mean?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: To defend the lines reached in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, how were you able to defend them if you were already there defending them, in essence, by being there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: In case of an attack, you couldn't go back. That's why it says odsudno, "decisive."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, for those of us who have not been in battle, could you please tell us, if you had a second echelon, perhaps even a third echelon, of men behind you in an event that this line broke to make sure that the enemy did not go all the way to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, it goes on to say that it will: "Secure the introduction of attack forces along the lines of the attack." "Secure the introduction of attack forces along the lines of attack," what does that mean?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: I have already answered in part. It means to demine in front of the defence lines sure passages for introducing forces for an active attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Does this mean that you are introduce the active forces?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Not me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So if -- well, who was going to then? If not you, who then?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: In active combat operations, southwards, the wolves of the Drina took part under the command of Milan Jolovic, the Drina Wolves, and a battalion from the Zvornik Brigade, under the command of Vinko Pandurevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. So in other words, this first sentence, if we are to understand it correctly, means basically hold your line and open up a passage, demine a passage, for forces to come?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, I want to go to the next line. It says: "With its auxiliary forces, it will attack along the Pribicevac/village of Lovine/Kvarc/Divljakinje axis." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you. First of all, could you please tell us what auxiliary forces are we speaking of when it says "of its," meaning the 3rd Battalion's, "auxiliary forces?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, what does it mean? It says: "With its auxiliary forces, it will attack." Did you have auxiliary forces?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: It was a Red Beret platoon attached to the 3rd Infantry Battalion at the end of June 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And it says that it was going to attack along the Pribicevac village of Lovine and Kvarc and Divljakinje. And I apologise for not being able to pronounce these rather difficult places. First of all, did this occur? Did you do this?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would you please tell us first of all, since we're speaking about the Red Berets and you said that there was one platoon, how many Red Berets were attached to the 3rd Battalion at that period of time.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: About 25.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And who was the komandir or komandant of this platoon?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Platoon komandir Rade Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would you please tell us whether they were located by the 3rd Battalion during this critical period, and we're talking about July 6th and onwards to July 11th, 1995. Were the Red Berets located and attached and working alongside with you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us exactly what they did.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: About 25 men, which means two squads. One squad went towards Lovine; one towards Divljakinje. In principle, they were forward observers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: How far from your line were these forward observers located?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Between 50 and 100 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And why were they placed there? I know you said "forward observers," and I don't want to lead you here, but tell us exactly what was their function.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Just to thwart the attack by the opposite side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us how heavily armed, what sort of equipment, artillery equipment, mortar equipment, you know, any -- what exactly did they have with them in order to maintain their positions?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Just light infantry weapons; that's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, we heard the term "Red Berets" before, and some of us conjure up images -- you know, certain images. Could you please tell us how well trained these Red Berets were and how well disciplined they were.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: I assume that you have the Red Berets as a professional army, but these were not professional ones. They were secondary school pupils, graduates or not. They had joined together under that name, and such names as youth and enthusiasm. So they were guys without any training. And Rade Petrovic in 1992 was a secondary school pupil but he never graduated from the fourth year of electrical engineering school, and he was their komandir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Is he related to Sreten Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Yes, his son.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And who is Sreten Petrovic? We've heard his name in this courtroom as well. Who is he?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Sreten Petrovic was my deputy, that is to say, the deputy commander of the 3rd Infantry Battalion. Otherwise, he was a miner by profession.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And was Sreten Petrovic there on the line during those critical days?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Yes, until the 9th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You may not need to shout into the mike. I think it kind of picks up, so you can just speak normally if you're not accustomed to it.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: I understand, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm not being critical. I just -- all right. Now, we're going to speak more about the Red Berets, but getting back to where we were 5.3, paragraph 5.3 on exhibit 406. If I understand it correctly, this was not accomplished, as it's stated in the combat order, is that correct, that they were to attack?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Yes. It's -- you can't attack a company or a reinforced company with a squad; that's completely mad.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, if we go to the next paragraph it says: "The tasks." And it says: "To rout the enemy along the lines of attack; reach the line of Divljakinje," and it has the points, Olovine, 831, "in the preceding task of the TT 789," and so on. Was this task completed?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, why not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: We stayed exclusively at the defence lines; whereas, the development of events on the southern side did not give any intimations for us to move. And the order from Commander Blagojevic was exclusively defence, decisive defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, the next paragraph says: "Responsible for the link-up with the 2nd Battalion." Was this accomplished? Did you link-up?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Yes. And before the operations, we linked up with the 2nd Infantry Battalion, and that is standard practice in the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And then it says: "The KAG, corps artillery group, will support it." Did the corps artillery group support you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: No, there was no need.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But were they there nonetheless, just in case you needed the support?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, do you know where they came from?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: From the corps command at Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Do you know who their commander was?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you have any contact, any communication, any coordination with them during that period?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And then it says the IKM will be in Kula. Is that where you had your forward command post during that critical period?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: The forward command post at Kula was the defence line, and it was held until the active operations started. That means nothing special.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, could you please tell us how far the 3rd Battalion under your command advanced, advanced - how much ground you gained - from your position to Srebrenica from July 6th to July 11th, the day when Srebrenica fell.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Not a single metre.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I want to go day by day now. Did anything unusual happen? Did you see any action? Were you fired at or did you fire upon on the 6th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Not the 3rd Infantry Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, what about on the 7th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What about on -- what about on the 8th of July?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Was there any action on the 9th of July?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Could you please explain to us what happened on the 9th of July. How your battalion specifically was involved, engaged, confronted, what have you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: On the 9th of July in the early morning hours, sometime between half past 4.00 and 5.00, an all-out attack started from the Srebrenica enclave directed to the south side of the 3rd Infantry Battalion, which was in contact with the Drina Wolves and the Zvornik Battalion. At one point during a fierce attack, we became separated and there was risk of the enemy forces getting into the rear of our troops. That is, to take positions behind our backs. At that point, we were engaged in active defence. So -- this lasted for a couple of hours. After a couple of hours, we managed to join forces, that is the left wing of the 3rd Infantry Battalion, in cooperation with the Zvornik elements and the Drina Wolves, we managed to push the enemy back to their starting positions. This took place in the morning before noon on the left side, on the left wing, of our forces; however, during the afternoon hours from the direction of Divljakinje, a lesser-intensity attack started in which my deputy, Sreten Petrovic, was wounded together with two other soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, when Sreten Petrovic was wounded, could you tell us how severe were his wounds.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: They were not fatal, not as dangerous, but every wounding is serious. He had sustained two gunshot wounds in the right leg and the right arm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And what happened to Sreten Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Sreten Petrovic, together with the two others who had also been wounded, was taken to the area of Pribicevac and in an ambulance driven to Bratunac, where he was taken to the Zvornik health centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, during that period of time did you see a gentleman by the name of Djordje Pejic, if I have the name correctly, who was with the engineers or a deminer.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: I know who the individual is, but no, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, do you know what his tasks were, you know, what his function was within the brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: He was a commander of an engineer's company, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did his engineer's company come by that area at any point in time, if you are aware?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Not to my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Have you ever had any contact with this gentleman, you know, on a professional sense with respect to his demining or engineering capabilities or mining, whatever the case may be?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Very little. I think it only once and very briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did you form an opinion at that point in time as to this particular individual?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would you please share that with us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm just not sure how this is relevant, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: May we go into private session, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, just for the record, I said he was not credible. I said he had credibility problems and issues. As we discussed before, as me and Mr. Karnavas agreed, it's going to be incumbent upon the Court, I don't want to use that term Mr. Karnavas used, but look into the testimony of each of these witnesses. So I'm certainly not counting out a person just because he happens to get up and not be truthful about one thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think the positions of the two parties are very clear and they are all in the transcript. When we evaluate the relevant piece of the evidence, we'll take into account the submissions by the both parties. Should we move on?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, we were talking about, I believe, 9 July 1995 and you told us that there was some particular action on that day. What about the 10th of July?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: On the 10th, the 3rd Infantry Battalion remained on the line that they had taken possession of; whereas, the rest of the units continued on their attack on Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, when you say "the rest of the units," we're not speaking about your units but the other units that were engaged by the Drina Corps and the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's what I said. The 3rd Infantry Battalion remained on the line that they had taken in 1993, and other units, and I was referring to the Zvornik Battalion, and the Drina Wolves continued with the attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would you please tell us about July 11th, the day that Srebrenica fell. How far did your troops, the 3rd Battalion of the Bratunac Brigade, advance towards Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Not 1 metre.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: It probably had to do with the assessment of the command. With two companies, I didn't have enough strength to move forward, that's one reason; second, it was necessary to protect the corps communications centre and it was also necessary to protect the medical corps and a couple of armoured mechanised vehicles that were in the area of Pribicevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did your commander, Mr. Blagojevic, did he issue you any orders on that particular day with respect to movement or lack thereof?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: The fall of Srebrenica took place on the 11th at around 1400. On that day an order came from Colonel Blagojevic, the commander of the Bratunac Brigade, and it read: "Remain at your positions until the communications centre and the medical corps, as well as the armoured mechanised units are back."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Just a second. I want to go back to an earlier question because we may need some clarification due to the translation. I asked you a question: Why didn't you move a single metre, why didn't you move from your positions? Could you please restate your answer, if you recall exactly what you told us.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: The order of the commander of the Bratunac Brigade read: "Remain at your starting positions until further notice."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And why was that, if you recall? What was the reason?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: The reason was the following: Upon entry into Srebrenica of the other units, at Pribicevac there remained the communications centre, the medical corps, and a couple of mechanised -- armoured mechanised vehicles, a mortar unit of the 3rd Infantry Battalion, the communications centre of the 3rd Infantry Battalion, logistics, the warehouse, the depots of the battalion. One simply couldn't move forward towards Srebrenica and leave all of that behind unprotected in the middle of the meadow.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Was that because of the number of companies that you had available to you at the time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: No. Even if we had had more companies, someone would have had to stay behind to provide protection, so I don't think that was the reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, as a result of this particular order, could you please tell us: How long did you hold your position?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: We held the position until the 13th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, when you -- and when you received this order from your commander, did you and the commander have some problems, so to speak?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I should say disagreements. Could you please tell us or describe to us what and why.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: It's very simple. The 3rd Infantry Battalion was mostly 70 to 75 per cent made up of the population -- of the local population of the Srebrenica municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So what?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: This meant that every soldier, including myself as the commander who on the 9th of May was expelled from Srebrenica and on the 15th of May evicted from my native village, and after three to three and a half years, obviously I wanted to see my home. I wanted to see my house, which was the case with all of the members of the 3rd Infantry Battalion. So more or less, that would be the essence of this problem. I don't know to what extent I'm making myself clear, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, let me see if I can figure it out. Is it that for three and a half years, having been expelled from your houses, being able to see them basically from your positions now that the line was free, you could not go to the houses --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Perhaps Mr. Karnavas can find another way to phrase the question because now he's just testifying. It's entirely leading and inappropriate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm merely summarising for the Court's convenience and trying to get the gentleman to clarify his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I believe that you have to ask your question step by step.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I know your gist in this question, but you have to lay out some foundations and then go step by step.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Want you to go back and explain your earlier answer a little bit. You said that you had been expelled from your house or your homes around the 15th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now it's July 19 -- July 11th, 1995. First of all, could you please --

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us that location, was it a Muslim location? A Serb location? A mixed -- an ethnically mixed location, where you had been expelled from, you and your men?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: The municipality of Srebrenica is a multi-ethnic municipality; whereas, the individual locations were uni-ethnic, except for the town itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What about the villages where you came and some of your men came from, were they all multi-ethnic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: No. The individuals were separate. There was one -- there would be one Muslim and one Serb village.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And from the period of May 15, 1992, to July 11, 1995, how many Serbs were living in the Serb villages?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Not a single one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Who had ethnically cleansed those villages?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: The BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: How close were those villages to your line, the line that you held for some two to three years, where the 3rd Battalion was located of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Depends. Some were located 500 metres in front of the line, and some, such as mine, 5 to 6 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And when was the first time that you and your men were permitted to leave the line to visit your homes and your villages where you had been ethnically cleansed from?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: In the afternoon of the 13th of July, whoever was able to -- I mean who lived closer by was permitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And what was the disagreement with your commander, Mr. Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: The soldiers wanted to enter together on the 11th and to visit their homes and apartments within the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: When was the next order that you received from your commander? When was it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, generally speaking, I do not interfere into your direct examination, but as you did before, I believe you have to ask some questions about the form of the first order, whether this gentleman received any order on paper or by courier or by radio communication so that we know there exists the order like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would you please, sir, answer the President's question. That order that you received on the 11th to maintain your positions and not to go away from your positions, was it oral, was it written, was it by courier, was it by radio, was it by telegram? How was it conveyed to you? Or did the commander come personally to visit you, to tell you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: I think that I received it at Pribicevac directly and personally from Colonel Blagojevic on the 11th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Where is Pribicevac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: The village of Pribicevac is located on the eastern slopes of Srebrenica, or to be more precise, midway -- rather, in the middle of the area of the 3rd Infantry Battalion. I cannot remember the exact elevation point, but it was a Serb village. And that's where the command of the 3rd Infantry Battalion was located.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Was anything else located in Pribicevac from the 6th of July to the 11th or 12th of July, other than the command of the 3rd Infantry Battalion?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would you please tell us what that was.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: The corps communications centre. I think that the commanding officer of the communications centre of the corps was Major Jevdzevic or Jevdzo. And there was also the command of General Krstic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would you please tell us about what time it was that you went to the command post in Pribicevac on the 11th.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Sometime in the afternoon. I'm not sure about the exact hour. It was a long time ago, but I'm sure that it was in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: How did you get there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: On foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Who else was with you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: My courier, who was with me all the time at my forward command post.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And your forward command post was exactly where during this critical period?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: 2 and a half to 3 kilometres south -- to the south. Javorov Vrh or Brdo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, during this period from the 6th to the 11th, did you have any means of communications between yourself and, say, your commander?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: No, apart from regular reporting. I did not take part in active fighting, so there was no need.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But maybe I wasn't clear. Was there a way -- did you have any means of communicating with your commander, such as a telephone, a radio?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Which of the two?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: We had the RUP 12 equipment, with a communications person who was operating it, and a Motorola.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Just so we're clear, what is a RUP 12?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: It's a radio station.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, if you had a radio station and you had a Motorola, why didn't you just call Colonel Blagojevic and talk to him over the Motorola or over the radio? Why take the trouble to walk all the way to Pribicevac to meet with him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: I don't know how familiar you are with the chain of command and subordination, generally speaking. If you look at the command of Colonel Blagojevic of the 5th of July --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And that would be exhibit 406. Is there a particular paragraph that we should look at?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 12, which reads as follows: Forward regular daily reports by 1700 hours and all other obligations coming from the commander, I'm duty-bound to receive personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. That's your understanding of the order or the practice?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Also in light of the practice in principle. It was possible for me to report on the situation to the commander, but from the commander back to me -- well, I don't think it would have been contrary to practice or to regulations, but in the military one is familiar with the usual types of procedures, usual reporting and issuing of orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, if we look at this report, or this order I should say, and we look at the tasks and the objectives, on July 11 - and you said it was about 1400 hours when Srebrenica fell - could you please tell us whether your tasks or whether -- with respect to this particular order, the tasks in the order, whether they had been completed or not.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: If you mean the overall orders --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes. This one, this particular one. Now that Srebrenica had fallen, was this the overall objective? Had it been met? As far as the 3rd Infantry Battalion is concerned, yes, it did carry out its orders. And the order was to stay at the positions reached and to defend the positions from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would you require another order before you could leave that position, or could you on your own decide, well, based on this particular order from the commander I have my tasks, Srebrenica has fallen, now I can just go home, dismiss the men, have them go greet their families, go visit their homes?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What is required before you can leave your positions?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: What is required is that you know where the next position is going to be, where to take up your next positions. And of course, that is something received from the brigade commander. So I would personally receive my following assignments from the brigade commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And did you receive any other assignments after this one?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: If I remember correctly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Could you please tell us what was your next assignment, that is after the one that you had received on the 11th, and that is to maintain your positions, not to move, not to advance, to Srebrenica. What was the next assignment?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: On the 13th, we were supposed to cross -- to go across Srebrenica, if I can put it that way, and to take up positions in the Bojna region, which is the north or rather south-west, it's the south-western side of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. I want to show you what has come in as an exhibit, P483. It will be 483/B in Srpski. If you could please look at this. First of all, do you recognise what this document is?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And could you please tell us what is it.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: It's an order for a ground search or search of the terrain.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And what is the date of this particular order, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: The 14th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, could you please tell us which paragraph on this particular order relates to your battalion.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would you please tell us what is being requested of you in your -- of your battalion in paragraph 3 of this order dated July 14, 1995.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: It says to search the terrain around Obli Vis up to Gradac, up to Zvijezda, to the left, Zeleni Jadar, Slapovici, Siljato Brdo, and the command post of the battalion in the Bojna region.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: This area which you're being asked to search, is that in your vicinity, the vicinity of the 3rd Battalion of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Zeleni Jadar, yes; Slapovici, relatively; Siljato Brdo is quite far off, but it is my native village, where the ethnic Serbian belt was about 20 kilometres longitudinally and 11 in depth; the Bojna area was the command post and the Serbian belt.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Could you please tell us whether this task that was being ordered of you and your men was carried out.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: When you asked me about the certain misunderstanding between me and Blagojevic, that is to say, my superior commander, it referred to this region. This area in the military sense -- actually, the terrain was not searched in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Because every soldier or group of soldiers, depending on whether they lived in Viogor, Orahovica, Tura, whether they went to their homes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Could you please describe to us normally what is the procedure when searching a terrain, how is that done.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: In the military sense, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Search of the terrain means the development, or rather, my battalion's dispersion all around and advance in the rear, in depth.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Does that mean -- if I understand you correctly, does that mean that you walk in single file on a path?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: In this case, yes, and more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So the normal way, the proper way, of searching the terrain is walking in a single file. Do I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: No. One beside another, breadth-wise. Yes, that way, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And for the record, I'm spreading my hands and advancing forward. Why would you do it that way? Why would you search the terrain in that fashion?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Well, if there are any stragglers, groups of stragglers or individuals, sabotage units, reconnaissance units, that kind of thing, smaller groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Of the enemy, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, in this particular case, if I understand your earlier testimony, it wasn't done in this fashion, is that correct, in the proper military fashion?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: No, but I don't think there was any need for that either.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, why don't you tell us why it wasn't done in the proper military fashion and why you think there wasn't any need of it.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Because these were exclusively Serbian villages and Serbian areas and regions, which in 1992 were set fire to and destroyed. And it would have been difficult to survive in an area like that, even for the best-trained sabotage units.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And so how was the searching of the terrain done? If it wasn't done in the proper military fashion, how was this task accomplished?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: From the Jadar area. Every soldier knew that he was supposed to come to the Bojna area towards evening. And anybody could, at their own will, go to their own homes and their native villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, was this some sort of an arrangement so they could carry out the order and visit their native villages as well? Is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Between me and them, yes. That was the only way I could muster them in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, what about Colonel Blagojevic's order? Was he aware of this, that this was being done?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you by any chance afterwards inform Colonel Blagojevic how his order had been carried out, so that at least he would know that his order was properly carried out pursuant to proper military procedure?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Well, the battalion in the Bojna area was there in the evening. And in life, the superior officer need not know everything if it wasn't at anybody's expense.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, I want to show you what has come into evidence, Prosecution Exhibit 485, 485/B is the Srpski version. Would you please look at this document. Could you please tell us what the document is.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: This is the first time I see this document, just like the previous one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. But could you please tell us from looking at it what it is, if you know, if you can tell.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: As far as I can read this handwriting, I can see that this refers to a platoon, and it says a Red Beret platoon. And it was sent to the Milici area at 1600 hours with the task of joining up there, et cetera, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Before we get to that on paragraph 2, my question, my concrete question, to you is: What is this document? Sir. Mr. Zekic, would you please tell us by looking at the top of the document what it is.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Well, nothing. It's a similar order to the previous one, and it says to search the terrain in the area, and so on. I find it difficult to read.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, perhaps we can let you look at this over the break, at least in the translated version it says it's a daily combat report dated July 14, 1995. Do you see that anywhere on this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Perhaps we can have a break at this point in time, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, it's time for a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And the gentleman can look at the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And we'll resume at quarter to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. Zekic, I trust you've had an opportunity to look at that document a little more closely, and I'm referring to what has been marked as P485. If I can go through that document step by step. Is that a daily combat report?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And the date of it, am I correct in stating that it is 14 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, we were talking about or you mentioned earlier about paragraph 2. And it states there, and I'm going to read the translated version. It says: "The Red Beret's platoon was sent at 1000 hours to the area of Milici to join the task in the direction of Zepa." Now, in the handwritten version that you are reading, the copy of the original, does it state 1000 hours or is it 1600 hours?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So that would be 4.00 in the afternoon, 4.00 p.m.?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, first of all could you please tell us whether these were the same berets, same Red Berets, same platoon of Red Berets that were there at the line with you from the 6th to the 11th that went off towards Milici, assuming that this daily combat report is correct. Are they the same Red Berets?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: I assume so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Were you aware that they had gone off to Milici?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you know with whom they had set off?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, we've heard testimony that Novica Pajic, a major, I believe, was an individual that had gone in that direction with some members of the Bratunac Brigade on that particular day. Do you know that gentleman?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And could you please tell us who that individual is.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Novica Pajic is a major within the composition of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What was his position, do you know?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: I think he was an operations man.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I think he was an operations man.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, you were asked about this individual when you gave your statement back on 29 November 2001, which would have been a couple of years after Mr. Blagojevic was indicted and after he was arrested. Now, at that time you were asked questions about Mr. Pajic. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you had indicated him to be - well, for lack of a better term - an alcoholic, one who consumed and after a couple of ounces of rakija, he was done because he had consumed a lot of alcohol. And that nobody -- he wasn't taken seriously. Now, when you made that statement to the Office of the Prosecution, was that a correct assessment, to your knowledge, of this individual's character?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: They asked me my personal opinion, so that is my personal opinion, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And that personal opinion was formed based on your observations and experience with this particular individual?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: As far as I knew him, and I have to say that I spent little time in that brigade composition with those men. So I didn't know people to a great extent personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But that was your opinion of this particular individual, this officer?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, in this daily combat report, there is no mentioning of anyone within the Bratunac Brigade coming across any Muslim men, soldiers, stragglers, whatever they be, during any searching operation. My question to you, sir, is: When you and your men set off to conduct that search operation pursuant to the order that we just went through earlier, albeit, it wasn't quite a searching operation pursuant to proper military procedure, did or your men come across any Muslim men?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: No. Neither.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Did you come across any dead bodies in that area?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did you come across any weapons that might have been left behind or dropped or what have you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would you please tell us what weapons, if any, were located and where perhaps, if you recall.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Yes. A 155-millimetre cannon, positioned in the Viogor area; and it had special optic sight geared towards our positions, and they were quartz. Javorov Brdo, Pribicevac, that area, and they had 99 per cent precision for this area of the battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Do you recall whether that cannon, that 155-millimetre cannon, had been fired during that period, that is from the 6th of July to the 11th of July?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And how do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: We had a 155--millimetre cannon, too, at Pribicevac. And it was -- and the two cannons targeted directly at each other, cannon against cannon. When I say "we," I don't mean the 3rd Infantry Battalion or the brigade, I mean the cannon that arrived from the corps. It was a 155-millimetre cannon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, that was the 14th of July. Could you please tell us what you did, if anything, on the 15th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Well, in principle what we did on the 14th, we did on the 15th and the 16th as well. So that means that I made use of the psychological rest period of the soldiers and when they toured their own homes and properties. But we could say that it was also a search, because from the area of Bojna to the village of Osedak and Cumavici was 5 and a half or 6 kilometres. So they would have traversed the area. So while it wasn't a classic search of the terrain, they would pass by that way and tell me whether there was anyone or nobody. So it was a two-way sort of feedback process.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And during that period, the 15th and the 16th, did anyone inform you whether they had come across any prisoners?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you have any means of communication with these various groups that were setting off in various directions searching the terrain?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Not with the groups, however in each of these -- in a couple of groups I would have one communication device, which was the Motorola.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did each of these groups have a Motorola or just you and some of them?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: No. Just the komandirs of the companies had Motorolas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, during that period of time did you have any contact with Colonel Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: I don't remember. It's possible that there was a report or two, but there were no special official contacts. But the reports were very brief, like everything is okay. Simply, there was no need for any other communication.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, during that period of time, say from the 11th or the 12th of July and onwards, where were you staying at night?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: I had certain obligations because I had spent May and June at the hospital of the military academy in Belgrade. One of my toes had been amputated. And it was necessary for me to visit regularly the health centre in Bratunac, or rather, the infirmary in Bratunac. So I probably spent every other night at home during that period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, during the period of the evening of the 12th and the 13th, in particular, did you become aware at any point in time that there were Muslim men in buses in Bratunac as well as in the Vuk Karadzic school and perhaps in another building?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Not on the 12th, because I was at Pribicevac. However, on the 13th, yes, I did have some information to this effect. But how many and what, no. But I had a vague idea that something was happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, when you say that you had some information, was that information conveyed to you by someone, or was that something that you personally observed and formed an opinion?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Not personally. They were just conveyed to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And when this information was conveyed to you, did anyone tell you what the plan was, what was expected to happen of those individuals that were kept in buses or in schools?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Didn't you ask, since you were -- you know, you and your family, I presume were living in that area, didn't you ask: What's going to happen with these people? Why are they -- doing in the middle of the town?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Now, if we go back to the order issued by the commander, Blagojevic, it was my assumption that they would be treated in accordance with Geneva Conventions. I was to a certain extent aware of the contents and the meaning of the Geneva Conventions, and I considered those people to be prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Since then - let's just get this out of the way - have you heard whether those people were treated in accordance with the Geneva Conventions?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: A certain number of people, yes, according to the information that I have. But others, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. When we say "others" what are we talking about? A small percentage of the men that were separated in Potocari, that were taken to Bratunac? Or are we talking about a large percentage? So what is it?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm objecting to this. It's obviously leading in nature, and I think that Mr. Karnavas can certainly formulate his question in a non-leading fashion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I don't think so. I think the answer of this witness is very weak. It is the responsibility for the counsel to clarify this issue. Maybe you could put your question another way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I will, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us, sir - and I believe you were asked this when you were in Banja Luka - but could you please tell us: What have you heard with respect to those people that were captured, the men, the Muslim men? And could you please give us an approximation of the figures that you heard.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: My initial information was that the prisoners would be leaving for Tuzla. At that time while I was at Pribicevac, I wasn't aware of what was going on in Potocari. I did not know that people were being separated at Potocari. I wasn't aware of anything at that time. Later, when I arrived in Bratunac, I received information to the effect that 2 to 3.000 able-bodied men were being held at the Vuk Karadzic elementary school, but that they, too, were supposed to go to Tuzla. And that was all I knew at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Since then, have you heard what has happened to those people?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And what is that, sir? What is it that you heard?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: I do not recall the date, but it was during that period of time. I know that genocide was committed in Kravica against a number of people; whereas, a number of people were taken towards Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, when did you learn about Kravica? And I presume that we're speaking about the incident at the Kravica agricultural warehouse?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you tell us approximately when it was that you heard of this atrocity.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: It would have been most probably sometime around the 14th or the 15th of July. But again, I'm not sure of the dates. But it was during that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, we talked about the 14th, the 15th, and the 16th. So now we're on July 17, 1995. Would you please tell us what, if anything, or what, if any, orders did you receive on that particular day; and what, if anything, did you and your men do pursuant to any orders that you might have received on that particular day?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: One day - again, I'm not sure about the date - one day I took part in the search of the Glogova/Sandici area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, how many days did you actually search? Let's stick with -- start with that.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: One.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Could you please tell us who else was searching the terrain when you were out there.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: The 3rd Battalion -- actually, what remained of it, one half of it, which was still located in the area of Bojna. The other part of the battalion took part in the search, and we had additional 30 to 40 people who were performing their work obligation; namely, that is people of limited physical capacities, either because they were elderly or some other reason. So it was in that area to my right, when looking to the Bratunac/Glogova/Sandici/Konjevic Polje communication. A gentleman was also taking part in this activity; I saw him for a couple of minutes only. He told me his name was Jevic or Jevric. So this was my first and my last encounter with this gentleman.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, let's stick with this particular gentleman. Now, do you recall which unit he was with?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: No. But they wore camouflage uniforms. They were well-dressed. But again, I don't know which unit he belonged to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. But would it be fair to say that he was the commander of that unit? Was he commanding the unit? Or was he just one of the members of the unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: If you're referring to his unit, yes. He was probably a unit commander, but I don't know exactly what formation this was, what kind of unit they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did you notice any other officers from the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: If you're referring to active-duty personnel, no. But the coordinator on behalf of the brigade was Mico Gavric. And then there was myself -- or the 3rd Battalion, which was directly subordinated to Mico Gavric.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, the -- so if I understand your answer correctly, Mico Gavric was your superior for this particular task?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, physically in what condition were you in in that period, in that particular day, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Generally speaking throughout that period of time, ever since from the 25th or 26th of June up until September, I moved around with difficulty. I had had surgery on my leg. The tendons had to be connected. So I moved very slowly, and all the time until we returned from Zepa, sometime in August. So I had a lot of difficulty moving around throughout that period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In light of your physical condition, could you please tell us whether on that particular day you were with your men carrying out this searching operation.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: In a command sense, yes, but not in the actual search.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please elaborate a little bit. What do you mean by: "In the command sense, yes, but not in the actual search"?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Well, in many cases it is perfectly normal for the commander or the commanding officer to be part of his unit. Due to my physical condition, I could not be with the members of the unit. I was -- to the side of my unit, I was using the Glogova/Sandici route. I had a driver, and I was moving around in an ambulance with my driver.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And where was Mico Gavric at this time, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Mico Gavric was to my right. And once we received the tasking, I didn't see him anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. What about the other gentleman that you referred to, Jevic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jevic was also to my right, the area of Hrncici and Lolici, thereabouts. So he was not with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Do you know whether you had been given any instructions by Mr. Gavric, who was your superior at that point in time, as to whether you were to give instructions to any of Jevic's men, or perhaps even Jevic himself?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Not to Jevic, but to me, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, during that -- could you please tell us, first of all, about what time you started and about what time you finished.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: We started with the introduction sometime around 10.00. And we finished at around 1600. So we worked for about five to six hours, and I returned to Bratunac sometime around 6.00 or 7.00 p.m. The visibility was still very good because it was summertime.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us whether during that period of time when your men and the others were searching the terrain, whether any prisoners were taken.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Not by my people, but by Jevic's people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Do you recall what the figure was, how many?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: I think between 30 and 40 people, maybe 50, but that would have been a maximum, from what I could see.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, what happened to these prisoners?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Well, now I know more or less, but I didn't at the time. The prisoners remained below the Sandici/Lolici/Konjevic Polje road on a meadow.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you know what the plans were for these men? Where were they to be taken?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: In a brief communication, I learnt that they would be going to Bijeljina. And it was the first time that I actually learnt that there was something at Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, when did this brief communication take place and with whom?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: With Jevic personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, I take it before you set off for this searching operation, there must have been some discussion as to what, if anything, would be done with any prisoners that might have been captured?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us to the best of your recollection what, if anything, was discussed as to how these prisoners would be treated, what would be done, where would they go, who would take care of it, and so on.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: The order came from Mico Gavric, who was the coordinator on behalf of the brigade, and I received that order, whereby we were supposed to take -- bring the prisoners to the road and that they should be treated in accordance with Geneva Conventions, namely that no harm should be done to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And just if you could help us out here a little bit. Could you tell us where did this conversation take place?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: In the Sandici area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I take it this was an oral -- would you consider this an oral order, or was this just a discussion? How did you take that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: It was an oral order. There was no discussion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Were you familiar with the Geneva Convention by that point in time, in light of your training?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, let me -- oh, incidentally, was the commander of the 4th Battalion there, Radika Petrovic? Was he there on that particular day? Did you see him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Not with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. I'm not suggesting that he was there; I'm merely asking whether you saw him.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, let me show you a document which is Exhibit P503. Please look at it. Can you read it, sir? Is it legible?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Could you please tell us what it is.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: This is a daily combat report of the brigade commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, I want to focus -- and what is the date on it, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: 18th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, I want to focus your attention to paragraph 2. Please look at it. And I'll just read it into the record. It says: "During the day, our units, the 3rd Infantry Battalion, the 4th Infantry Battalion, and people mobilised for compulsory labour are searching the terrain in the area of Pobudje, Hrncici and Konjevic Polje." Is that what it says in your document as well?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, could you please tell us whether this was the area that was being searched by you and your unit on that particular day, if you recall.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Glogova, Sandici, Hrncici, yes; Pobudje and Konjevic Polje, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, you said Glogova, Glogova is not reflected on the English translation, but it's there on the -- in the handwritten version. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, let me show you another document. And this has been marked for identification purposes as D135. Please look at that. Do you recognise this document? Do you recognise what it is, I should say?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's a daily combat report of the brigade commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And what is the date on this, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: 19th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, if you could look at paragraph 2, there's some language there. And there is a part that says: "The 3rd Battalion is securing the road from the village of Glogova to Konjevic Polje." And then it states that they don't know what happened to the 4th Battalion. Now, with respect to the 3rd Battalion, on that particular day, July 19, 1995, were you and your battalion securing the road from the village of Glogova to Konjevic Polje, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Glogova, yes; Sandici, yes; Konjevic Polje, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, when it says: "Securing the road," could you please explain to us what exactly that entails, what does that mean?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: In principle, it means a safe passage for civilian and military, also population on all of these communication lines, Konjevic Polje, Milici, Vlasenica, and others. So no activity whatsoever, just providing security to the passing traffic, no searches, nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, were any prisoners captured on that particular day? Did you come across any Muslim men who were trying to make their way to the -- to Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: No, not on that part. But we were located there. We did not have any searching tasks. We were just supposed to be there to provide security to the route.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So you were on -- well, tell us exactly where you were located, physically speaking. Was it the terrain? Was it the asphalt road? Was it somewhere in between?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Next to the asphalt road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us who it was that issued you that order, putting you in that location to secure that stretch of the road.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: If my memory serves me right, it was Major Eskic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us for how many days you were in that location carrying out that specific activity.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Until we left for Zepa, so the securing of the road in that area, and also we were in charge of the area of Bojna, just above Srebrenica, at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, on the 18th of July, 1995, did you by any chance see any buses in the area of I believe it's Lolici in the evening, buses full of Muslim men?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ZEKIC
utterances.text: Not on that day, I didn't see that.
